newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul to sell additional seven pct in Korea Telecom.
newsitem.headline: Seoul to sell additional seven pct in Korea Telecom.

text.p: The South Korean government plans to sell additional seven percent of its holdings in Korea Telecom (KT) to the public this year, a senior company official said on Thursday.
"The original plan was 14 percent for this year, but because stock market was not doing well, we cut the plan in half," Lee Sang-ho, director of KT's privitasation division, told Reuters.

The government currently owns 80 percent of KT shares and the public holds the remainder. The sales started in 1993. The government plans to reduce its holdings in KT to 51 percent as a part of a privatisation drive.

Lee also said listing of the state-backed telecommunications company would be delayed until 1997 because of the slugishness in the Seoul bourse. "The government does not want to rock the boat, so it is being careful," Lee said.
But Lee did not give the exact date of the listing.
After the relative failure of the first public auction of the telephone company's shares in 1993, the government pledged KT's listing in 1995.

Speaking to analysts and invstors at a Union Bank of Switzerland Korea investors forum, Lee said the government was in talks with the World Trade Organisation (WTO) to allow foreigners to buy shares in KT by 1998.
Currently, foreigners cannot hold any shares in the unlisted Korea Telecom. -- Seoul Newsroom (822) 727 5644
